en: The Hymn to Avalokiteśvara composed by the bhikṣuṇī Candrakāntā.

I bow to the one who bears the name Avalokita—the teacher of the world honored by the three realms, the excellent Brahmā praised by the lords of the immortals, the supreme king of sages, the bestower of splendor and accomplishment. (1)
He bears the beautiful form of a son of the Sugata, with a supreme body adorned with many marks;
he wears the Tathāgata Amitābha upon his crown, and his left hand is adorned with a golden lotus.
His matted locks were curved, pure, tawny, and smoky; his full face was as radiant as the orb of the moon;
his excellent eyes were long like lotuses; and the pair of his cheeks was as white as a fragment of snow. (3)
His lower lip was equal to the lotus-navel of Viṣṇu; his voice was like the thundering of autumnal clouds;
his pair of arms was adorned with many jewels; and the palms of his hands were as delicate as young, tender grass.
His left body was wrapped in a deer skin; his trembling lower lip was adorned with beautiful earrings;
his navel region was as pure as the interior of a lotus; and he wore a golden, excellent girdle embellished with jewels.
Wearing a beautiful, variegated cloth wrapped around his waist, he has reached the further shore of the great ocean of the Jina’s enlightenment;
having acquired the boon through the accumulation of much merit, he removes the affliction of fever and bestows abundant happiness. (6)
He brings about auspicious peace, he is the creator of the three realms of existence; he moves on earth and through the sky, bearing a body of praise.
He has utterly conquered the forces of Māra in their various confusions, and he brings about the ultimate reality of the ten perfections.
Dedicated to the solitude of the square abode, awakening the realization of the non-duality of suchness;
with a pair of feet resounding like jeweled anklets, possessing the slow, measured gait of an elephant and the grace of a swan. (8)

He who has attained steadfastness through the acquisition of the fullness of great nectar, whose constant abode is the ocean of the milk-waters, who delights in dwelling upon the glorious Mount Potalaka, and whose beautiful eyes are pure and composed of compassion. (9)
The Praise of the Blessed Lord Śrīmad Āryāvalokiteśvara, composed by the nun Candrakāntā.
